sections.content:
Population change in Camden in 2032

The population in Camden is projected to increase from 217,365 people in 2022 to 245,651 people in 2032.

The biggest factor in this population change is net international migration, which will increase the population by 74,086 people.

This is different to the majority of areas in England, where net internal migration is projected to be the biggest factor in population change.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Camden
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Camden, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More births than deaths mean that the population is projected to increase by 12,194, with 24,991 births and 12,797 deaths in Camden between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would increase the population in Camden by 5.6%, compared with an increase of 6.0% in London and an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to reduce the population by 59,822, with 283,516 people moving to the area and 343,338 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Camden by 27.5%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to increase the population by 1,762, with 8,453 people moving to the area and 6,691 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Camden by 0.8%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 74,086, with 133,841 people moving to the area and 59,755 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Camden by 34.1%, compared with an increase of 14.7% in London and an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Camden in 2032

The median age in Camden is projected to remain the same at 33 years between 2022 and 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 12% of the population in Camden are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 11% in 2022.

sections.title: The 20 to 29 age group are set to see the largest change in Camden between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Camden is projected to stay the same, at around 74%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 148 to 149 over the same time period.

This is below average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Camden?

In 2032, 17% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 18% in 2022.

This is below average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in Camden between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will stay around the same, at 5%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will stay around the same, at 6%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will fall from 7% to 6%
